newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-INDIA BEAT AUSTRALIA IN FIRST TEST UNDER TENDULKAR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA BEAT AUSTRALIA IN FIRST TEST UNDER TENDULKAR.

text.p: Sachin Tendulkar failed with the bat but won his first test as captain on Sunday as leg-spinner Anil Kumble helped India to crush Australia by seven wickets on the fourth day of their one-off test.
India lost three top batsmen, including Tendulkar for a duck, in their short 56-run victory chase after bundling out Australia for 234 in their second innings.
The tourists avoided an innings defeat thanks largely to a defiant 67 not out by Steve Waugh.
India were all out for 361 on Saturday in reply to Australia's first innings total of 182 on a dry and cracked wicket.
With Australia's star leg-spinner Shane Warne absent through injury, Kumble had centre stage to himself.
The Indian recorded his seventh five-wicket haul in a test innings when he took another two wickets in the first session to finish with five for 67 and an overall match haul of nine for 130.
Waugh put on a brave show as he added 41 runs for the ninth wicket with tailender Peter McIntyre to remain unbeaten on 67 made in 273 minutes off 221 balls with five fours.
Waugh became the first Australian batsman to score 50 in the match when he square drove Kumble to the fence.

Resuming at their overnight score of 168 for six, 11 runs in arrears of India's first innings lead, Australia suffered a jolt when Kumble had left-hander Brad Hogg caught by Rathore at forward short-leg for four.
A short time later Kumble trapped Reiffel leg before wicket for six with the total on 191.

After lunch, when Australia were 232 for eight, medium-pacer Venkatesh Prasad cleaned up the Australian tail, trapping McIntyre leg before wicket and getting Glenn McGrath to edge a catch to Nayan Mongia behind the stumps.
Paceman Paul Reiffel made early inroads into India's second innings, bowling Vikram Rathore for 14 and trapping man-of-the-match Mongia, who made 152 in the first innings, lbw for zero.
Tendulkar, who made 10 in the first innings, also lost his stumps when paceman McGrath found a gap when he was on zero.
But Saurav Ganguly and Mohammed Azharuddin each scored 21 to help India reach their victory target easily. Ganguly struck three fours and Azharuddin five.
